notes: Resolution order (AC#3): valid stored value wins -> per navigator entry (exact culture match, then primary-subtag) in caller preference order -> DEFAULT_LOCALE ('cs-CZ'). DECISION (WI left implicit): iteration is PER-ENTRY exact-then-subtag, NOT two global passes. So ['de','en-US'] -> 'de-DE' (the user's first preference wins over a later exact), matching standard language-detector semantics and AC#8 intent. Pinned by an explicit test.

Subtag map is DERIVED from SUPPORTED_LOCALES (code.split('-')[0] -> code) via a Map built at module load; the ONLY hardcoded literal is the legacy tl->fil-PH (Tagalog) alias, which is not derivable. A hypothetical 7th locale (es-ES) auto-detects from 'es' with NO edit to resolveInitialLanguage.ts (AC#8). resolveInitialLanguage.ts is on WI-8's AC#8 whitelist for exactly this tl alias.

languageStorage: key 'app.language', NOT in authStorage (survives logout — device preference). Mirrors driverSettings.ts try/catch: getStoredLanguage swallows getItem throws -> null; setStoredLanguage swallows setItem throws -> no-op. Validation is SUPPORTED_LOCALES.some(l => l.code === value) — registry-derived, no hardcoded code list.

useLanguage: uses const { i18n } = useTranslation() so `current` re-renders consumers on language change (react-i18next). setLanguage = i18n.changeLanguage + setStoredLanguage + document.documentElement.lang = code (AC#5). No reload. A benign React act() warning appears in the useLanguage test (react-i18next's languageChanged re-render lands just after the awaited changeLanguage) — same tolerated pattern as the existing renderHook precedent; tests pass and lint is clean. Left as-is rather than over-engineering.

applyInitialLanguage.ts is the only impure wiring (reads navigator.languages + getStoredLanguage, resolves, changeLanguage, sets <html lang>). Called ONCE from main.tsx ONLY, never from index.ts — index.ts keeps static lng: DEFAULT_LOCALE so the ~1,464 existing unit tests stay Czech. Verified: no test file and no non-main module imports applyInitialLanguage.

Playwright pin (AC#7): added locale: 'cs-CZ' to the TOP-LEVEL use block only. The three projects (chromium, mobile-driver, mobile-customer) do NOT override locale, so it applies to all — Chromium navigator.language becomes cs-CZ and applyInitialLanguage() keeps every existing e2e spec Czech. Did NOT run e2e (Phase 5 covers it, per task).

AC#6 format guard (formatStaysCs.test.ts): this test has NO genuine RED — money.ts builds Intl.NumberFormat('cs-CZ') at module load and never reads i18n; analyticsRange.ts uses a fixed Europe/Prague tz. It is a non-goal REGRESSION guard (spec §21), not a red-green cycle: it actually switches i18n to de-DE mid-test before asserting formatCzk(1200) still yields the cs-CZ nbsp-grouped '1 200 Kč' and defaultThisMonthRange stays Prague-anchored, then restores cs-CZ. It bites the day someone wires Intl.NumberFormat(i18n.language) or a UI-language date formatter into either module. Money nbsp is U+00A0 (verified via node), asserted with the money.test.ts \s-normalization idiom. Date target chosen: defaultThisMonthRange (the only Prague-anchored shared date fn) — asserted identical + fixed value across the language switch.

Language restored to cs-CZ in afterEach of BOTH useLanguage.test.ts and formatStaysCs.test.ts (the two suites that changeLanguage) — the one thing that could turn the full-suite Czech baseline red if vitest isolation weren't perfect. Full suite re-run confirmed green (1487).

TDD honesty: each of the three pure/hook cycles was written test-FIRST and RED was observed (module-not-found transform error) before implementing to GREEN. Order followed rules/web-testing.md#test-ordering: pure (resolveInitialLanguage, languageStorage) -> hook (useLanguage) -> guard (formatStaysCs).

AC#8 / WI-8 forward-compat: three new NON-whitelisted production files (languageStorage.ts, useLanguage.ts, applyInitialLanguage.ts) + edited main.tsx all derive from SUPPORTED_LOCALES/LocaleCode with ZERO hardcoded non-default culture-code literals, so WI-8's extensibility.test.ts (flags {en-US,ru-RU,uk-UA,fil-PH,de-DE} outside its whitelist) stays green. The single locale-code literal introduced by WI-2 is tl->fil-PH, which lives in the already-whitelisted resolveInitialLanguage.ts. Kept literal-free by design.

Confirmed via grep: applyInitialLanguage is imported ONLY by main.tsx (the index.ts occurrence is a code comment, not an import); no test or provider module imports it, so component tests keep the static cs-CZ baseline. lint re-run standalone: EXIT=0 (--max-warnings 0).
No CLAUDE.md fact appended — no new non-obvious trap surfaced (the cs-CZ U+00A0 grouping and the money.test.ts \s-normalization idiom are already established in the codebase).
